planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Schnickel Fritz forms a dormant diploid clump that benefits from a sustained winter chill.

directions: Bred by David Kirchhoff and registered in 1996, Schnickel Fritz is a dormant diploid daylily bearing fully double, near-white blooms with a soft green throat, held on compact 16-inch scapes in the early-midseason with strong rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 2004, prized among white doubles for its clean form. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Layers of Gold forms a vigorous clump with extended bloom and reliable rebloom.

directions: Bred by David Kirchhoff and registered in 1990, Layers of Gold is a double-flowered daylily bearing medium gold self blooms with a green throat, measuring about 5 inches across on 24-inch scapes with extended bloom and dependable rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1999 and has since been used widely as a parent for gold double tetraploids. Divide crowded clumps every three to four years in spring to keep plants blooming vigorously.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Siloam Double Rose forms a dormant diploid clump with fragrant, extended blooms.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry of Siloam Springs, Arkansas and registered in 1979, Siloam Double Rose is a dormant diploid daylily with fragrant, extended double blooms in bright rose with a ruby-red eyezone and green throat, reaching about 6 inches across on 20-inch scapes. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1986, one of many honors earned by Henry's prolific Siloam series. Divide clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Cabbage Flower forms an evergreen diploid clump, so protect foliage from hard freezes in colder zones.

directions: Bred by David Kirchhoff and registered in 1984 from a Twin Crown x Nagasaki cross, Cabbage Flower is an evergreen diploid daylily with fragrant, fully double pastel lemon-yellow blooms and a green throat, held on 17-inch scapes in the extra-early season with good rebloom. Its unusually ruffled, cabbage-like double form helped it win the American Hemerocallis Society's Ida Munson Award for best double-flowered daylily in 1990. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Red Squirrel forms a semi-evergreen diploid clump with a long flowering period and reliable rebloom.

directions: Bred by J.R. Blanton and registered in 2005, Red Squirrel is a semi-evergreen diploid daylily bearing reddish-orange blend blooms above a gold throat, with 3.5-inch flowers on roughly 20-inch scapes in the early-midseason and a long bloom period with rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Annie T. Giles Award for best small-flowered daylily in 2015. Divide clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; George Jets On forms a dormant diploid clump with heavy branching and reliable rebloom.

directions: Bred by Yost and registered in 1999, George Jets On is a dormant diploid daylily with fragrant, ruffled rose-cream bicolor blooms featuring a yellow eyezone and cream-rose pencil-etched lines above a green-yellow throat, carried on 28-inch, heavily branched scapes in the early-midseason with rebloom. Its unusual coloring and form earned it the American Hemerocallis Society's Annie T. Giles Award for best small-flowered daylily in 2006. Divide clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Awesome Candy forms an evergreen tetraploid clump with fragrant, reblooming flowers.

directions: Bred by Patrick Stamile, Awesome Candy is an evergreen tetraploid daylily in his small-flowered Candy series, bearing fragrant yellow blooms about 3.5 inches wide with a bold cherry-red eye and picotee edge above a green throat, on roughly 25-inch scapes in the early-midseason with reliable rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Annie T. Giles Award for best small-flowered daylily in 2008. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.
